transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because I keep having these nights where I eat an amount of food that honestly scares me. I’ll start with just some leftovers after I finish grading papers, and then... I just keep going. I end up going through cereal, crackers, peanut butter, and even whatever snacks I had packed for my classroom. It's just a really huge amount of food, and it feels out of control.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever do anything to try to make up for the food or get rid of the calories, such as making yourself throw up or taking laxatives?

No, I don't make myself throw up or use laxatives or anything like that. But, um... after one of those nights, I do try to fix it in other ways. I’ll tell myself I’m not allowed to eat breakfast or lunch at school the next day. And then, after work, I’ll stay out running on the trail for hours, or I'll do extra yoga routines, even when I’m feeling really shaky and completely exhausted. I just feel like I have to work it off somehow.
Could you tell me what your current height and weight are?
I'm about 5'6", and... I think I weigh around 145 pounds right now. It fluctuates a bit, but that's usually where it sits.
On average, about how many times a week do these episodes of eating this way happen?

Um, on average... well, for the past few months, there has rarely been a single week without at least one night where I eat far more than I meant to. Usually, it's more than just once a week, to be honest. And then, you know, the next day I always try to make up for it by not eating at school, or pushing myself through a really long run or extra yoga.
How much does your body weight or shape affect the way you feel about yourself as a person?

It affects me a lot. Honestly, it pretty much dictates how I feel about myself. Like, if I notice I look even a little softer around my stomach, or... if my pants feel tight right before a staff meeting, I honestly feel like I’ve failed at everything. It really doesn't matter how well my students are doing, or how prepared I am for my lessons that day. None of that seems to count. If I feel like my body isn't right, I just feel like a complete failure as a person.
